name: Swordlord Dancer (Scout Archetype)
body:
Among the many masters of sword dueling, the swordlords are one of the well known schools. There is a subset that learns a cultural sword dance that was derived from the fighting style. These dancers are fluid movers, mobile, and masters of sword combat. While not as focused as their dedicated peers, the learned movements and agility are a great boon in a duel.

Weapon and Armor Proficiencies

A swordlord dancer is proficient with simple weapons and finesse blades.

This replaces the weapon proficiencies gained by the scout.

Sword Dancer (Ex)

Beginning at 1st level, the swordlord dancer adds 1/2 their class level to Performance (dance) checks. Additionally, they gain Weapon Finesse with all finesse blades.

This ability replaces trapfinding.

Duelist (Ex)

At 1st level, the swordlord dancer gains Combat Expertise and Dueling Mastery as bonus feats.

They need not meet the prerequisites for these feats though Dueling Mastery applies to all finesse blades, not just the dueling sword. Additionally, while using a finesse blade in one hand with their off-hand open, and have at least 1 grit point remaining, they may add their Dexterity bonus to damage dealt. However, if the swordlord dancer has levels in classes other than scout, the Dexterity bonus applied is restricted to the levels in scout. In all cases the Dexterity bonus applied in lieu of Strength.

This ability replaces the sneak attack gained at 1st level.

Stowed Readiness (Ex)

Beginning with 3rd level, So long as the swordlord dancer has 1 grit point, they are treated as possessing the Quickdraw feat usable with finesse blades only. Additionally if they have their finesse blade sheathed, it is counted as readied in their hand for the purposes of Dueling Mastery.

This ability replaces the scout’s initiative deed.

Steel-Wind Dance (Ex)

Beginning at 4th level, the swordlord dancer may attempt a DC 15 Perform (dance). On a success, they reduce the penalty to attack from Combat Expertise or defensive fighting by 1 until the end of your next turn. If employing both Combat Expertise and defensive fighting simultaneously, the reduction to the penalty is only applied once.

At 8th level and every 4 levels thereafter, the swordlord dancer may increase the DC of the check by 5 to reduce the attack penalties 1 further. For example, a 12th-level swordlord dancer can choose to attempt a DC 25 Perform (dance) check to reduce the attack penalty from one or both abilities by 3. If this check fails but exceeds the next lowest DC, the bonus is that DC’s bonus.

The Perform check is made at the beginning of combat when initiative is rolled or as a swift action on the swordlord dancer’s turn. The benefits of this ability only apply to finesse blades.

This ability replaces trackless step and the sneak attack gained at 4th level.

Terrifying Dance (Ex)

At 6th level, the swordlord dancer gains Dazzling Display as a bonus feat. Additionally, they can use Perform (dance) instead of Intimidate to demoralize enemies while in combat and using a finesse blade.

This ability replaces the sneak attack gained at 6th level.

Dueling Style (Ex)

At 7th level, the swordlord dancer gains Dueling Style as a bonus feat. Then, at 13th level, they gain Dueling Style Aegis as a bonus feat. Finally, at 16th level, the swordlord dancer gains Dueling Style Conquest as a bonus feat.

They need not meet the prerequisites for these feats and they treat their scout level as their base attack bonus for the purposes of qualifying for feats that specifically affect a weapon that qualifies as a finesse blade or is chosen with such a weapon, like Weapon Focus.

Additionally, their Scout level equals their fighter level for prerequisite purposes of the aforementioned feats.

Finally, any ability or feat that triggers on using a specific weapon that qualifies as a finesse blade, it is usable for all finesse blades.

This ability replaces the sneak attack gained at 7th, 13th, and 16th levels.

Shifting Blade (Ex)

At 8th level, the swordlord dancer gains Improved Feint as a bonus feat usable only with finesse blades. Additionally, they may use Perform (dance) instead of Bluff for feint attempts.

This ability replaces covert expert and hide in plain sight.

Counterattack (Ex)

At 10th level, a swordlord dancer may make an attack of opportunity against an enemy who hits them in melee, so long as the attacker is within the swordlord dancer’s reach.

This ability replaces the sneak attack gained at 12th level.

Masterful Bladework (Ex)

At 12th level, the swordlord dancer may attempt a feint as a swift action if only using a single finesse blade in one hand. Additionally, on a successful feint, the swordlord dancer may attempt to demoralize the target of the feint as a free action using their Perform (dance) skill.

This ability replaces the bonus combat feat gained at 12th level.

Masterful Defense (Ex)

At 19th level, when using Combat Expertise or fighting defensively, the swordlord dancer also gains DR 5/-.

This ability replaces the sneak attack gained at 19th level.

What is a Finesse Blade?

A finesse blade is any weapon from the heavy blades or light blades weapon groups that may be used one-handed with Weapon Finesse whether by weapon category, property or an ability or feat.

If going for the traditional Paizo intellectual property dueling school this class is based off of, the proper weapon is a dueling sword, but this class is open for more nimble masters of the blade regardless of discipline.
